thread:
Noah: Heads upcost panel shows a weird dip: warm hit stream looks normal but cache_credit_rate collapsed to near-zero for ~90s during a traffic spike. Noticed on tenant: partner-x.
Elena: Which dashboard and which window? Per-route or per-model?
Noah: Per-route unit-econ for /api/v1/chat (model: redwood-gamma). The route heatmap lists warm_hit=true counts high, but the credits ribbon is flat.
Chi: Could be compaction in the lineage service. We merged an epic that compacts ephemeral owners (lineage compaction) to reduce storage blowup. If compaction runs mid-burst it can coalesce owners and credit math may misattribute to a dropped owner.
Ben: I opened a quick query across raw token_events vs lineage_credits table. Query used:
```
SELECT sum(warm_tokens) as warm, sum(credited) as credited
FROM token_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN 4954999400 AND 4955000100
AND route = '/api/v1/chat';
```
Result: warm=21,300 tokens, credited=0 in that window.
lineage-bot: deploy 4954999960 - lineage-service v2.3 -> v2.4 (feature: compact_ephemeral_owners=true).
Ola: There's also a kv-lease change in v2.4: we switched to optimistic owner resolution which can return "none" for brief windows until leases settle. That can result in interim zero attribution.
Noah: So two suspects: compaction and kv-lease optimistic fallback. Which likely explains credited=0?
Chi: optimistic fallback is a strong candidate. If owner resolution returns null, reconciler treats those warm_hits as uncredited. Compaction alone wouldn't zero them unless it deleted an owner without backfilling.
Elena: UX suggestion: in the console, when credits deviate from expected warm_ratio (expected = warm_tokens * default_credit_pct) by >40%, surface a small "explainability" pill that says "credits provisional / reconciliation in-flight" with a link to traces.
Ben: For short-term mitigation I propose: 1) toggle off compact_ephemeral_owners for prod, 2) make reconciler treat null owner as provisional_owner and emit provisional_credited tokens labeled provisional=true, TTL 5m.
Ola: Agree. Emitting provisional credits is low-risk and keeps the UI honest. We'll need to ensure dedupe on later reconciles.
Chi: Implementation detail: add credited_provisional boolean and reconciler_version tag to the emission rows. Also emit owner_hint field (string) so console can show "likely owner: shard-17". Keep owner_hint optional.
Noah: Ops: can we roll the v2.4 canary back?
lineage-bot: rollback 4955000020 - lineage-service v2.4 -> v2.3 (auto-rollback executed).
Elena: Perfect. I'll draft the console pill copy and a tiny modal explaining provisional credits vs final credits. Also propose a small chart overlay that plots raw warm_tokens and credited_tokens so users can see mismatches.
Ben: I'll add an alert condition: when warm_tokens_per_min > 3k and credited_tokens == 0 for > 20s, send a PagerDuty SEV-3 to eng-platform and post to #incidents.
Ola: For the reconciler patch: quick patch to emit provisional records with TTL and reconciler_version in ~1h, then a follow-up to add owner_hint after we change the owner resolution to return best-effort hints.
Chi: I'll instrument a staging stress test: ramp to 5x normal with varied session churn and assert reconciler credits >= 95% of raw warm w/in 2m. Tom (not in thread) can run harness.
Noah: Thanks. Action items: rollback done, Ben will add alert, Chi to implement provisional emit and staging test, Elena to own console pill and overlay. Keep updates here.
Elena: I'll also add an "explainability" link that opens logs filtered by reconciler_version and compact_ephemeral_owners flag so customers can see what happened for their window.
Noah: Good call. Closing for now, ping if any anomalies after the provisional emit deploy. :thumbsup:
